title: Swap a blown fuse in a hinged DIN-rail fuse holder for a new one taken from its carton, and latch the holder shut
instruction: The panel is locked out and tested dead. F2's fuse has blown: replace it with a new 6 A fuse from its box, put the blown fuse in the parts tray, and close F2.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00; about 821,000 US jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) "Repair or replace wiring, equipment, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools". Replacing a blown control fuse is everyday panel work, and in modern panels the fuse sits in a finger-safe modular holder: the electrician pulls its carrier open by the grip tab, lifts the blown fuse out of the carrier's clips, takes a new fuse of the rating on the legend out of its carton, lays it into the clips and swings the carrier shut until it latches.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A gray steel wall-mount enclosure, 20 x 16 x 6 in (50.8 tall, 40.6 wide, 15.2 deep), stands on the bench with its open front toward the robot at x 27.3 and its door off; its back pan faces the robot at x 40.8. A 35 mm top-hat DIN rail runs across it at height 15. On the rail stand three gray Eaton Bussmann CHM1DU one-pole modular fuse holders (7.39 tall, 1.75 module, 8.32 deep off the rail, fronts at x 31.73), F1 at y 4.5, F2 at y 0, F3 at y -4.5 (2.75 cm of bare rail between neighbors, room for the fingertips), plus six terminal blocks further right. Each holder's front is a hinged carrier, 6.0 tall and 2.0 deep, hinged at its bottom front edge (height 12), with a red grip tab on top (1 tick on F1's tab, 2 on F2's, 3 on F3's); it holds a 10 x 38 mm fuse upright between two end blocks with contact clips. F2 holds a blown Bussmann KTK fuse (marked with a black stripe round its middle). On the bench lie two opened Bussmann cartons of 10 x 38 mm fuses (10.8 x 4.3 x 1.3, lids folded back flat behind them): KTK-6 (6 A, blue band) centered at x 16.5, y -12 with three fuses left, and KTK-10 (10 A, black band) at x 16.5, y 12 with two left, lying side by side across the carton, pointing at the panel. A blue parts tray, 15 x 10 x 3, sits at x 20, y -30. Both arms start at their ready pose. One fixed layout.
scoring: 0 for the trial, whatever was reached before or after, from the second control step in a row at which F1 or F3 is open 5 degrees or more, a 10 A fuse lies seated in F2's clips, or the blown fuse lies seated in them again after it had been out (a real trial: the side camera and a check of each carrier and of the fuse in F2 afterwards). Otherwise, from the final state: 1.0 with a 6 A fuse seated in F2's clips (both ends within 1 mm of the clip floor), F2 shut (within 2 degrees of flush with the holder's face), the blown fuse in the parts tray, released (a release check: no gripper in contact with F2's carrier, the new fuse or the blown one, contact meaning its own shape within 2 mm) and both fuses still (under 2 cm/s for the last second); 0.75 with a 6 A fuse seated in F2 and the blown fuse out, the rest not done; 0.5 with the blown fuse out of F2 and a 6 A fuse out of its carton; 0.25 with the blown fuse out of F2, or F2 open 30 degrees or more; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. A real trial: overhead and side video throughout; after it, a straightedge and 2 mm feeler across the holders' faces (shut or open), the overhead photo (blown fuse anywhere in the tray, a 6 A fuse anywhere outside its carton), then F2 opened by hand to read the fuse's printed catalogue number and to check that neither ferrule moves further into its clip when pressed lightly. Where the arms end up is not scored. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Open F2 by its tab, lift out whatever fuse is in it, put the black-striped (blown) fuse back in its clips with both ferrules pressed onto the clip floor, and swing F2 shut until it latches; lay a straightedge across the three holders' faces to check all are flush; put each fuse back on its pencil mark in its own carton (read the printed catalogue number); cartons and tray back on their tape outlines; arms to ready.
fidelity: Real sizes. Each carrier is a hinge with a latch law (a spring within 6 degrees of shut, 0.05 N*m at its edge, about 1 N at the tab) and a stop lying level (90 degrees; both assumed). F2's clips are their fingers and end blocks as colliders plus a law pressing each ferrule to the floor and the clip's middle with 0.8 N (assumed; reaction on the carrier) until 2.5 mm out. Cartons and fuses are free rigid bodies; nothing attaches a fuse to a hand.
